title: MongoDB NoSQL Injection in Login Authentication
description:
The /login endpoint is vulnerable to NoSQL injection attacks via MongoDB operators in JSON request body. The application directly passes user-supplied JSON data to MongoDB queries without proper sanitization. When MongoDB operators like $ne, $gt, $regex, $nin, and $exists are sent in the username or password fields, they are interpreted by the database instead of being treated as literal string values.

The application uses Express/Flask with MongoDB backend and processes JSON POST requests with username and password fields. The backend fails to validate input types or escape operator characters before constructing database queries. Instead of treating username and password as strings, the application passes raw JSON objects to the MongoDB query engine, allowing attackers to inject query operators.

This represents a fundamental failure in input validation and query parameterization, allowing attackers to construct arbitrary MongoDB queries that bypass authentication logic.
impact:
CRITICAL - Attackers can bypass authentication by injecting MongoDB operators. This allows:
1. Authentication bypass without valid credentials - accessing any user account
2. Unauthorized access to admin accounts and privileged users
3. Complete compromise of the authentication system
4. Potential for data exfiltration through operator-based queries ($regex, $where, etc.)
5. Lateral movement to other system functions protected by the compromised authentication

The vulnerability is exploitable without any special privileges or valid credentials, making it an immediate critical risk. Attackers can gain full system access by simply sending specially crafted JSON operators to the login endpoint.
